title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: BENNY'S HOUSE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Benny Castillo, a valet parker at a hotel in Reno, Nevada.
For six years, he parked other people's nice cars.
Then he bought the ugliest house on Pine Street. A raccoon came with it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE DOUBTS
segments.quote: Nothing will ever be attempted if all possible objections must be first overcome.
segments.author: Samuel Johnson
lines: The roof sagged. The porch leaned. Everyone said walk away.
His mom said, Mijo, the raccoon pays more rent than you will.
But his grandpa kept a line from Samuel Johnson taped to his fridge:
Nothing will ever be attempted if all possible objections must be first overcome.
Benny signed the papers. The raccoon did not.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE LIST
segments.quote: Rome was not built in one day.
segments.author: John Heywood
lines: That first weekend, Benny wrote a to-do list. It had two hundred jobs on it.
He wanted it all done by Thanksgiving.
His buddy Omar laughed, and quoted an old proverb John Heywood wrote down:
Rome was not built in one day.
So Benny did one job a day. Monday, a window. Tuesday, a doorknob. Wednesday, the raccoon moved out.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE NEIGHBOR
segments.quote: Whatever is worth doing at all, is worth doing well.
segments.author: Lord Chesterfield
lines: Next door lived Ruth Kemper, seventy-four, a retired carpenter.
One day she knocked on his wall. A whole sheet of drywall fell over.
She said, My dad used to quote Lord Chesterfield:
Whatever is worth doing at all, is worth doing well.
So Benny tore it out and did it again. Slowly. With Ruth holding the level.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE STEPS
segments.quote: The physician can bury his mistakes, but the architect can only advise his client to plant vines.
segments.author: Frank Lloyd Wright
lines: By spring, Benny built his first porch steps. He measured twice. They came out crooked anyway.
He wanted to sink right through them. Ruth just laughed and quoted Frank Lloyd Wright:
The physician can bury his mistakes, but the architect can only advise his client to plant vines.
So Benny planted a grapevine on the railing, and called the steps rustic.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE PIPE
segments.quote: Every noble work is at first impossible.
segments.author: Thomas Carlyle
lines: One cold December night, a pipe burst. Water everywhere. Benny sat on a bucket, ready to sell.
Ruth brought coffee and an old book by Thomas Carlyle, the Scottish writer:
Every noble work is at first impossible.
At sunrise, they fixed the pipe together. Ruth called him a plumber. Barely.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE PARTY
segments.quote: We can only be said to be alive in those moments when our hearts are conscious of our treasures.
segments.author: Thornton Wilder
lines: A year later, Benny threw a housewarming party on the crooked steps.
His mom raised a glass and read a line from the American writer Thornton Wilder:
We can only be said to be alive in those moments when our hearts are conscious of our treasures.
Benny looked around. The house was fine. The people were the treasure.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Start anyway. One job a day. Do it well. Laugh at mistakes. Keep going. Count your people.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Start anyway. Do one job a day. Do it well. Laugh at your mistakes. Keep going. And count your people.
I once hung a picture in my study. It's still on the floor.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
